contamination_regulatory_regime: Environmental Protection Act 527/2014 ch.14: the polluter must clean; if the polluter cannot be found or does not, the area holder who consented to the pollution or knew or should have known of the area's state when acquiring it must clean it, unless obviously unreasonable; otherwise the municipality (s.133). Assessment reports go to the Permit and Supervision Agency (s.135). Soil condition data sit in the national MATTI information system (about 29,000 areas recorded, over 7,000 remediation decisions).
known_contamination_notes: Sotkamo hosts the Talvivaara-Terrafame nickel-zinc mine (opened 1 October 2008 by Talvivaara; Talvivaara went bankrupt and Terrafame acquired the site in 2015, per Terrafame's own history page). Its environmental record was not checked against a regulator source. Outokumpu is the site of a former copper mine (the municipality is named after it). Ilomantsi has a gold-mining zone under municipal planning (Southern Gold Line partial master plan).
source: Finlex 527/2014 s.133-135; Terrafame history page (terrafame.com); Municipality of Ilomantsi
gaps: The MATTI register itself and the SYKE/ELY records for Sotkamo and Outokumpu were not opened; the mine's contamination and leak history was not verified against a regulator page and is deliberately not asserted here; the Outokumpu mine fact is from a secondary source; whether MATTI entries are public per site was not verified.

contamination_regulatory_regime: Code de l'environnement L125-6 and L125-7: the State publishes secteurs d'information sur les sols (SIS), annexed to local urbanism documents; a seller or landlord of land in an SIS must inform the buyer or tenant in writing, with remedies if pollution makes the land unfit for the intended use; the map of former industrial sites is flagged in certificats d'urbanisme.
known_contamination_notes: Corrèze SIS layer (DDT19, 2020-2021 vintage, WFS opened 2026-10-04): 18 SIS in the département, 2 inside Parc communes: 'Salamanière' (Peyrelevade) and 'Le Jacquet' (Davignac), nature not stated in the layer. Creuse and Haute-Vienne SIS, BASOL/CASIAS and former uranium mine records (MIMAUSA) and radon potential on granite were NOT opened (Géorisques unreachable from the research host).
source: Code de l'environnement L125-6, L125-7; DDT19 'Secteurs d'Information sur les Sols (SIS) en Corrèze' (data.gouv.fr)
gaps: Two of three départements not checked; uranium legacy and radon not verified for the perimeter.

contamination_regulatory_regime: Maine DEP Uncontrolled Hazardous Substance Sites Program (38 MRS ch. 13-B, 1361-1371; the state equivalent of Superfund), Brownfields program and a public Hazardous and Oil Spill reporting system; private wells are not regulated and owners test and treat (Maine CDC).
known_contamination_notes: No county-specific contamination finding was opened. Statewide facts: Maine CDC says 1 in 10 Maine wells has too much arsenic (arsenic MCL 10 ppb), and recommends testing private wells annually for coliform, E. coli, nitrate and nitrite and every 3-5 years for arsenic, uranium, radon and others. Maine's PFAS farm problem is tied to licensed biosolids spreading sites (MFT and MOFGA run PFAS testing grants; Indigenous producers of food and medicine need not meet commercial-farm criteria); no Washington County tally was found. Blueberry-barren pesticide use was not documented against a primary source.
source: Maine DEP Uncontrolled Sites Program; Maine CDC Arsenic in Drinking Water and Private Well Water; Maine Farmland Trust PFAS page
gaps: Washington County arsenic rate, PFAS site list, uncontrolled-site list and blueberry-barren pesticide record not opened; burden rated from the statewide private-well position.
